My scratch script is C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-User--claude-spares-spare-7RIe5m\bbf7f24a-a450-4563-b7aa-b8bcef60bc6e\scratchpad\stage6\refute-physneural0\ch.py. The physiological premise is wrong, though. The §5.5 I0 values (AMH II ≈ 46, AMH I > 53, C 41–49, QST 43–47) are surface stimulus temperatures. §11.9's θ_heat is the temperature at the terminal. Tillman et al. 1995 (J Physiol 485:753) used the same diffusion approach and found that the temperature at the receptor (mean depth 150 µm, stepped stimuli) is far lower than the surface temperature at threshold: about 40.2 °C for C mechano-heat nociceptors. Treede et al. 1995 give type II AMH a median surface threshold of 46 °C, but a mean response latency of 120 ms to a 53 °C laser step. With the document's own model (α 1e-7, d 150 µm, monkey base 38 °C), a terminal threshold of 43 °C reproduces that 120 ms exactly. A terminal threshold of 46 °C predicts 290 ms, which the data rule out (scratch lat.py in the same folder). So the document's single θ 43 °C at the terminal is consistent with the Aδ evidence, and the 250–350 ms EMG target does not rest on a mismatch. Fix (a) would move the reflex to ≈ 0.49 s by putting surface thresholds at the receptor depth. Its core sentence, 'Transduction starts when T_rec reaches the class threshold θ_c … AMH II 46 °C, AMH I 53 °C', would add that same error. The alternative of a 100 µm default depth contradicts §6.10's argument from thick glabrous skin. Option (b) is not wrong, but its rationale ('I0 values scale intensity only') misses the real distinction. The improvement actually worth making is wording only: state in §11.9/§12.3 that θ_heat is a terminal-level threshold, different from the surface I0 values in §5.5, and cite the Treede 1995 latency and Tillman 1995 for it, instead of 'heat threshold 43 °C per §5'. A separate point, not raised by this issue: Treede 1995 found only type I AMHs in monkey glabrous skin. That puts in question §5.5's 'type II carries first pain to heat' when applied to the palm, although Iannetti et al. 2006 report Aδ heat responses from human glabrous skin.

rejected.claim: Cortisol on immune cells: neuroendocrine ∧ neuroimmune; brake_C uses g.neuroendocrine · g.neuroimmune; neuroimmune off: 'glucocorticoid action on immune cells' off
rejected.reason: Refuted. brake_C = 1/(1 + b_C·max(0, cortisolRel − 1)·g.ne·g.ni) (L4443) acts only on cortisol above basal, so there is no basal glucocorticoid restraint for the neuroimmune gate to remove. A product of gates cannot double count. With neuroimmune off, the cytokine → PVN edge is cut, cortisol does not rise, and brake_C ≈ 1 with or without the g.ni factor. The +31 % IL-6 AUC is therefore the loss of both brakes (vagal and cortisol), as the A.5 Neuroimmune row states, not an artefact of the extra factor. Putting glucocorticoid action on immune cells inside the neuroimmune network is a documented design decision: the A.5 Neuroimmune row lists it, and A.8 #3 names the cortisol brake as an AND gate. The proposed fix is wrong: braking only the cytokine-driven cortisol increment would remove the brake from stress-driven cortisol, which does suppress cytokine responses.

calibrations.param: contact-heat thresholds: cold θ 45 °C, warm θ 33.5 °C
calibrations.rationale: Both follow the doc. 45 °C is the paradoxical cold-fibre discharge threshold (§5.6; Dodt & Zotterman 1952, cat) and 33.5 °C is skin baseline 32 °C plus 1.5 °C, the middle of the +1–2 °C warm detection threshold (Rolke et al. 2006 [recalled]). On the §11.9 erfc model at 55 °C and 150 µm they give 340 ms and 33 ms. The only fault is the uneven treatment of the Aδ nociceptors, which still use 43 °C instead of AMH II 46 °C or AMH I 53 °C (issue 1, §6.10).
calibrations.suggested: Own the values in §5.6 and in a new per-class θ table in §11.9: cold 45, warm 33.5, C polymodal 43, AMH II 46, AMH I 53 °C. Put the 55 °C onset times (340 / 33 / 224 / 429 / 9,434 ms) next to the §12.3 sensitivity table.

calibrations.param: startle recruitment delays: neck 68, shoulder 85, arm 115, leg 150 ms
calibrations.rationale: These are [model] central delays added to the reticulospinal conduction. The simulated EMG onsets (5 % of peak) are SCM 87.5, trapezius 89, deltoid 109.5, biceps 140, quadriceps 195 ms. All fall inside the §6.11 bands (neck 75–121, shoulder 100–121, arm 125–195, leg 145–395 ms). The ordering matches Brown et al. 1991 (SCM first, caudal later). The bands have no primary source and may be movement (film) latencies, not EMG (issue 4). The leg onset sits in the lower half of a very wide band, and the elbow joint movement (199 ms) just exceeds the arm band.

calibrations.rationale: Ditunno et al. 2004 define four phases of reflex return (areflexia, initial return, hyperreflexia, spasticity). They do not describe resting sympathetic tone, so tying ρ to those windows is a modelling choice. The 'one third to a half of rest tone' justification rests on plasma noradrenaline, a spillover measure. Microneurography shows resting sympathetic traffic below a complete cord lesion is low or absent and mostly reflex-driven (Wallin & Stjernberg 1984; Stjernberg, Blumberg & Wallin 1986 [secondary summaries only]). Chronic vascular tone recovers through receptor supersensitivity and intrinsic tone. ρ should be a vascular-tone surrogate, not firing.
calibrations.suggested: Own ρ in §7.8 with a cross-reference from §6.15. State 'ρ = spinal and intrinsic vascular tone fraction, not resting sympathetic firing (low or absent below a complete lesion on microneurography); phase windows borrowed from Ditunno et al. 2004 for timing only', [model], low. Keep the numeric values.

calibrations.suggested: [0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15] for muscle, splanchnic and cardiac channels; skin channels up to 0.3 at phase 4
calibrations.rationale: Direct recordings in complete cervical or high thoracic lesions show almost no spontaneous muscle sympathetic activity below the lesion. The remaining activity is reflex-driven and sparse, though skin vasomotor activity may be higher. The 'third to a half' comment fits plasma noradrenaline, which has other sources. The late-phase exaggeration should come from reflex gain (the dysreflexia surge), not from resting tone. Owner section §7.8, with §6 for the phase index.

The §8.13 value of 1.8 kcal/min is right. The B formula as written (multiplier 1) lets delivery overshoot r_set by about 50 % (≈ 2.7–2.9 kcal/min), finishes a 600 kcal meal in 3.7 h and fails the 2 h Tougas window (25 % retained against 30–60 %). A multiplier of 16 gives 1.81 kcal/min, 6.05 h, and 77/52/10 % retention at 1/2/4 h. Put 16 into the §8.8 formula and treat B's weights (0.5/0.3/0.2) as the share of the brake that each network supplies. The 4 h retention then sits at the 10 % edge, which needs a small k₁/k₂ re-tune.

calibrations.rationale: The 45 °C value is the paradoxical discharge of cold fibres (Dodt & Zotterman 1952, cat), already in §5.6. 33.5 °C for warm receptors is just above the 32 °C contact baseline and consistent with warmth detection thresholds of about 1 °C. calibrations.param: startle recruitment delays: neck 68, shoulder 85, arm 115, leg 150 ms
calibrations.rationale: The order matches the brainstem-to-caudal progression of the auditory startle (Brown et al. 1991; sternocleidomastoid first, caudal and distal muscles later). Neck at 68 ms is a little later than the roughly 55 ms sternocleidomastoid onset in a related free-fall study (54 ms). The leg value of 150 ms is plausible but posture-dependent (tibialis anterior is about 40 ms earlier when standing than sitting). Tag the four values [model, low], cite Brown 1991, and state the posture. Outside my lens, so not checked beyond this.
